HarHarVeryFunny 2026/11/13 07:40
As has been said many times, this is not a normal IPO meant to raise funds for a growing company. This is a liquidity/exit event to let investors, founders and employees realize paper gains.

It hard to say they are doing this now because they need the money now - they are committed to spending close to $1T ($1000B) on datacenters/etc, and the IPO will only raise them around $50B (5% of what they need).

The timing seems more decided by the fact that growth may never look better than it does now as tokenmaxxing gives way to customers looking for ROI and cheaper alternatives to frontier LLMs, such as decision models and non-frontier LLMs which are rapidly becoming good enough for many use cases.

They would only be losing money until 02031 if they sold one trillion dollars of bonds in the near future, at 15% yield (something like 45% higher than what they're currently paying). This would be an unreasonably bad way for them to fund several years of datacenter construction. In fact, it's roughly the worst possible way. Anyway, I have been typing from my phone, so here is my admittedly back of napkin math. Anthropic has $450 billion in near to medium term commitments (through 2030) and another 500 billion after that through 2040 or so, most if not all of which they cannot cancel. So just in per existing commitments they owe already 110 billion+ per year for the next 4 years. I don't know if that is front loaded or back loaded, or evenly spread, but that is the average. That likely does not include all of their costs such as their 3.2 billion annual marketing spend, employee costs, and other annual costs such as their debt servicing which we will put at 6.3 billion per your math, all of which is undoubtedly going to grow. So they need at least 125-150 billion a year minimum for the next four years just to keep the lights on. That is not profit; just break even.

From a revenue growth standpoint they went from 144% QoQ revenue growth in Q2 to 44% QoQ revenue growth Q3. I don't think we can ignore the downward trajectory of their revenue growth. And there are signs that the revenue growth story might get a lot worse in the short term as competition gets more fierce and with companies becoming more discretionary on AI spending meanwhile the cost of computer continues to rise. Short term 15% is probably realistic sustained QoQ growth and after that 5-10% Medium term.

I think this is an overly negative take. The IPO is mostly primary issuance and the cash goes to the company. This extends Anthropic's runway into years rather than months. Crucially, this means revenue growth does not need to reaccelerate and can be allowed to slow to something resembling a healthy technology company.

The IPO has to happen ASAP because financial conditions are deteriorating for Anthropic and private capital has tapped out. They will need cash, they're out of people to get it from, and the cost to get it goes up every day.

I agree the fundamental question of whether Anthropic can grow past its fixed commitments is still a big unanswered question and that there are a lot of fundamental headwinds that you correctly brought up. But at least the IPO takes the business as it exists today seriously.
